touches.text: Tool: a complete primitive. Has users, not an owner. Calls no other Cairn component (stdlib and base only) and owns no state of its own. Lives in cairn/tools/ (17). Its data for a holder lives under that holder: ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/tools/<tool>/.
A device's code lives in cairn/devices/<device>/; its data in ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/.
The instance is a number; a singleton is 0. A bare name addresses instance 0 (`cc` means `cc 0`); the number is written only when it isn't 0.

Akien 2026-11-13, said in akiendell's session, answering the same Q#93 on a second asking (verbatim): "no there's no conflict there. those are completely different kinds of things. spinning up a second ground loop should see the first, and that it's fine, and exit quietly. if we're starting a new one on purpose, like there's an older one running, we'll add --force, which means kill the old one. we change that intention. i have no recollection why it says loudly. but the naming, yes. if we had two zeros how would messages get routed? or <host>_cc_RESCUE? we DO want to be able to spin up more than one of something. many things can be singletons or not... like the embeddings generator. if we wound up with too much traffic, we might open a second on another host. but the launcher has to ask the shim to create the instance, and so it's the shim's job to say 'we've been asked to start and instance, then we've not been given a name for it, then we have a cc_0 instance, so I'll launch it with cc_1'"

An instance is declared by its folder existing in class-space: cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/ (one address in two roots). Declared = the folders (read by the rack tool, 17.20); running = which of those are in the rack.

The ground loop finds one pulse.py per device. pulse.py reads its own device's declared instances (5.7.3.4) and pulses each one, so the ground loop never needs to know instances exist. Pulsing an instance that isn't connected is what starts its shim.
A tool, not a machine, even though it spans several files; the base-most stuff belongs to Cairn.
rack: reads the declared instances, the device folders (5.7.3.4). USERS: the rack machine, pulse.py, the scheduler.
